summary: Redwood AE/SE walked Medexa through a migration-focused demo showing parity mapping from OpenAI/Anthropic/Together APIs to the Redwood API. Primary concerns were data residency, SOC2/HIPAA posture, performance/latency parity, function calling and streaming, and cost tradeoffs between hosted and dedicated. Agreed to run a benchmark pilot and exchange security docs.
topics: API parity: endpoints, params, function-calling mapping
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-23
Start time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Daniel Park (Medexa CTO), Sofia Alvarez (Medexa ML), Hannah Lee (Medexa Security), Tom Brooks (Medexa Product)

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, can you hear me ok?
[00:02] Daniel Park: yep, loud and clear, thanks Maya.
[00:05] Maya Chen: awesome, quick agenda — i'll do a high level on migration approach, liam will demo parity mapping for text/gen + function calling, priya will cover embeddings and console/optimize features, then we'll do q&a and next steps. sound good?
[00:14] Sofia Alvarez: sounds good. we mostly want to understand how much work to move from openai + anthropic to a single api, and implications for latency/cost.
[00:20] Liam O'Connor: cool, i'll share my screen — give me a sec while i open the mapping doc — all right, so first slide, high-level mapping: openai's chat completions -> redwood "chat.create" endpoint, messages map 1:1, system/user/assistant preserved. anthropic's assistant-style -> same mapping but note temperature/top_p differences in param names. together/other providers map similarly.
[00:38] Hannah Lee: can i interrupt — does redwood support function calling like openai's function_call? we rely on that heavily for structured outputs.
[00:44] Liam O'Connor: yes — Redwood supports function/tool calling and we've added a near-identical schema for name/arguments; the main differences are parameter names and the response wrapper. i'll show an example request in a second but gist is you can reuse your function definitions with minimal changes. sometimes the assistant roles or stop tokens differ so we include a small shim in the parity mapping.
[01:05] Maya Chen: quick note on infra: you can run on hosted first for quick testing, then move to Dedicated or Private (VPC/on-prem) if you need data isolation or HIPAA controls.
[01:14] Tom Brooks: medexa is sensitive — we've got PHI in some flows. can you cover encryption, kms, and audit logs?
[01:20] Liam O'Connor: absolutely — we have KMS integrations for both hosted (managed key option) and private (customer-managed keys/HSM). audit logs are exportable to your SIEM and we keep per-request metadata for traceability. redwood is SOC2 certified and we offer HIPAA-aligned contracts for Private deployments; i'll put the SOC2 + HIPAA docs in a follow-up.
[01:38] Sofia Alvarez: great. on performance — our main worry is inference latency for interactive flows. our current openai median p95 is ~280ms for 512-token responses. can you reach parity?
[01:46] Liam O'Connor: good question — parity depends on model choice and deployment mode. with our hosted API using optimized kernels we commonly hit comparable p95s for similar model families. for strict p95 targets we recommend Dedicated pools so you get predictable GPUs and no noisy neighbors. also we have batching, kv/prefix cache and quantization profiles that reduce cost while keeping latency constraints.
[02:08] Daniel Park: how much work is the code change? are there SDKs?
[02:11] Maya Chen: we have SDKs in python/node/go, and the migration doc shows minimal diffs: endpoint, small param renames, and token accounting changes (we provide helpers to translate token counts). most customers refactor 1-2 files for request plumbing and reuse existing prompt/tooling.
[02:26] Liam O'Connor: demo time — showing a live parity example.
[02:30] [screen share noise]
[02:34] Liam O'Connor: here is an openai chat request on the left, here's equivalent redwood chat.create on the right — notice messages[], role mapping, and function schema mapping. i'll run the request.
[02:45] [typing sounds]
[02:50] Liam O'Connor: response comes back streaming — you'll see the same incremental tokens. one difference: our stream framing includes a small status chunk when a tool call happens, but your existing client can handle it with a 4-line change.
[03:10] Sofia Alvarez: the streaming framing looks slightly different — would we have to rewrite our stream parser?
[03:14] Liam O'Connor: typically no, most teams update a small helper to normalize frames — i'll include a code snippet you can drop in.
[03:20] Hannah Lee: about logs — does redwood retain prompt text in logs by default? we need to redact PHI.
[03:25] Priya Rao: good point — redwood supports prompt redaction and configurable retention windows. for Private deployments you control retention and can enable automatic PII scrubbing. we'll share the exact config options.
[03:38] Daniel Park: embeddings — we currently use openai embeddings for semantic search. is there an exact match?
[03:44] Priya Rao: we support multiple embedding models and provide a parity table. in practice you pick a model with similar vector dims and then update your ingestion pipeline to call redwood embeddings endpoint. the response shape is similar; we added a compatibility layer for top-k similarity results.
[03:59] Tom Brooks: any differences in token billing? our finance team tracks tokens closely.
[04:03] Maya Chen: billing is per-token for hosted, with slightly different definitions of context vs. generation tokens depending on model; our parity guide includes a token translation tool that approximates cost differences. for Dedicated we do committed throughput pricing which can be more predictable.
[04:19] Sofia Alvarez: security question — SSO and RBAC, we need teams separated.
[04:22] Liam O'Connor: yes SAML/SSO supported, fine-grained RBAC, and per-route API keys if you want to isolate services. we also have audit trails at token/request level.
[04:35] Hannah Lee: do you support VPC peering? we need network isolation for PHI.
[04:39] Liam O'Connor: Private deployments support VPC and on-prem. For Dedicated we can do private network options and peering depending on region. we'll include the network diagram in the follow-up.
[04:52] Maya Chen: let's run a short demo of Optimize — smart batching and model suggestions. priya?
[04:56] Priya Rao: sure — showing the console: Optimize suggests batching size 8 for your request distribution and recommends a quantized variant for lower-cost throughput. you can preview quality regressions with our eval harness using a set of prompts — here's an example where 8-bit quantization increases latency slightly but reduces cost 45%.
[05:19] Sofia Alvarez: can we automate fallback to a higher-quality model if the quality metric drops?
[05:22] Priya Rao: yes — rollouts support automatic fallback policies and canary thresholds. you can set alerts based on eval sets and automatic rollback.
[05:32] Daniel Park: i want to confirm: if we run a pilot on hosted, will it be easy to move to Dedicated without changing prompts?
[05:38] Liam O'Connor: yes — the API semantics are the same; you change endpoint/credentials and pick the deployment. Dedicated gives you pinned model versions and capacity guarantees, but no prompt changes.
[05:47] Tom Brooks: licensing for HIPAA — will there be additional fees?
[05:50] Maya Chen: enterprise add-ons for compliance typically include Private deployment fees and support; we'll put a rough estimate in the pricing follow-up but it depends on the deployment mode.
[06:02] [background noise, 6 second pause]
[06:08] Sofia Alvarez: real quick, how do you handle conversational state/kv cache if we have multi-turn dialogs? we use a lot of prefix caching.
[06:15] Liam O'Connor: Redwood runtime supports KV cache and prefix caching; we map conversation ids to cache keys and can persist cache across requests for hot sessions — reduces tokens for repeated context. we also provide TTLs and eviction policies.
[06:32] Hannah Lee: any certifications beyond SOC2? we need ISO and contractual language for Business Associate Agreement.
[06:36] Liam O'Connor: we have SOC2 and are pursuing ISO; for HIPAA we offer BAA on Private deployments — i'll include the BAAs / legal contacts.
[06:49] Maya Chen: okay — let's go through a quick migration checklist i put in the parity doc: 1) map model IDs and params 2) update client to redwood SDK or REST 3) validate function-calling shim 4) run a small benchmark and compare p95/p50/cost 5) pilot with a sample prod workload.
[07:09] Daniel Park: sounds good. timeframe? we want to pilot in october.
[07:12] Maya Chen: that's doable — we'll prioritize SOC2/HIPAA docs and a benchmark window in early october.
[07:18] [interruption — dropped audio for 4s]
[07:23] Priya Rao: i'll coordinate with Sofia on the benchmark inputs — how big is the dataset for semantic search?
[07:28] Sofia Alvarez: about 1.2M documents, average 1.8k tokens per doc for indexing snippets, our queries are shorter.
[07:35] Priya Rao: good, for the benchmark we'll sample 1% and run embedding ingestion throughput and similarity latencies, and compare vector dims.
[07:44] Tom Brooks: any gotchas we should know about when swapping embedding models?
[07:47] Priya Rao: embeddings vector space differences matter for quality — we recommend a reindex and a validation set. Optimize can run A/B against the current vectors and provide drift metrics.
[07:59] Sofia Alvarez: do you provide a compatibility layer for our existing openai SDK calls? we have a bunch of internal wrappers.
[08:04] Liam O'Connor: we provide a compatibility shim and examples that mirror openai's responses; many customers run a small adapter in-house. it's usually 1-3 dev days depending on complexity.
[08:16] Hannah Lee: about key rotation and HSM — we need quarterly key rotation and HSM-backed keys for private.
[08:21] Liam O'Connor: supported for private; hosted has managed rotation options and customer-managed keys for dedicated/private. we'll add HSM notes.
[08:33] Maya Chen: ok we're near the end — quick recap and next steps.
[08:37] Maya Chen: next steps: maya will send parity mapping + sample snippet, liam will send SOC2/BAA info, priya will schedule benchmark, medexa to share peak RPS and sample data.
[08:48] Daniel Park: thanks — this was helpful. looking forward to the pilot.
[08:51] Maya Chen: great — thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email and close out action items.
[08:56] [meeting ends]
